name: Visto per lavoro subordinato (employer-sponsored work visa, Decreto Flussi quota)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from an Italian employer, who files the nulla osta (clearance) request via the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione during the annual Click Day window, competing for a fixed quota slot.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from an Italian employer prepared to file during the Click Day window.

requirements.blocker_text: Non-seasonal subordinate-work quota applications are open only to nationals of countries with a migration-cooperation agreement with Italy (roughly 35-39 countries as of the 2026-2028 DPCM, including Albania, Bangladesh, India, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Tunisia); other nationalities generally cannot use this specific quota channel.

evidence_required.document: Employer's nulla osta application filed during the Click Day window
Employment contract meeting sector-standard (CCNL) pay and conditions
Suitable housing declaration (dichiarazione di ospitalità/idoneità alloggiativa) from the employer

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years, tied to the employment contract, renewable

sources.title: Ministero del Lavoro e delle Politiche Sociali (lavoro.gov.it) -- 'Flussi 2026-2028, pubblicato il decreto da oltre 497mila ingressi,' confirming D.P.C.M. 2 ottobre 2025 (Gazzetta Ufficiale 15 ottobre 2025), the 164,850/165,850/166,850 three-year quota figures, and the Click Day calendar
Portale Migranti -- Decreto Flussi 2026: Click Day, quote e requisiti, citing D.P.C.M. 2 ottobre 2025 (Gazzetta Ufficiale 15 ottobre 2025) and Circolare interministeriale n. 8047/2025
Studio Legale Vallini Vaccari -- Decreto Flussi 2026, procedure, click day e precompilazione, listing eligible nationalities for the non-seasonal subordinate-work quota

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: Italy's non-seasonal subordinate work visa is fundamentally quota- and timing-driven, not merits-driven in the ordinary sense -- the D.P.C.M. 2 ottobre 2025 (Gazzetta Ufficiale 15 ottobre 2025, converted into Legge 179/2025) sets a total 2026 non-EU labour-migration quota of 164,850 across all channels, of which only 76,200 (or 76,850 per one source, a minor cross-source discrepancy not resolved in this research pass) is allocated to non-seasonal subordinate work. Selection is first-come-first-served by submission timestamp within the Click Day window (12 January 2026 for the main non-seasonal round), with sources describing demand routinely exceeding available slots within the opening minutes -- selection_method is modeled as 'first_come' rather than 'lottery' since it is literally a timestamp race, not a random draw, though the practical unpredictability for an individual applicant is similar. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no gov.it or Ministero dell'Interno page was directly fetched for the specific 2026 quota figures in this research pass -- both sources are specialist immigration-law consultancies citing the same D.P.C.M. and circolare, which is stronger than a single uncorroborated claim but still short of a direct primary fetch; a follow-up session should attempt integrazionemigranti.gov.it or the Ministero dell'Interno's own portal directly. Non-seasonal subordinate quota applications are further restricted to nationals of countries with bilateral migration-cooperation agreements -- a structural filter with no equivalent in most other work_sponsored routes in this dataset, closer in spirit to how EPS bilateral agreements gate Korea's E-9 route than to an open global work-visa market. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the general 5-year/10-year Italian tracks; it_family_reunion_visa, it_ancestry_jure_sanguinis, and it_eu_long_term_residence document several materially faster alternate paths this route's holders would generally prefer if eligible.
